shared_text:
The flight. A regional jet on a visual approach to an airport, in visual conditions.

The crew. The first officer was the pilot flying and the captain the pilot monitoring.

What happened. On the arrival, air traffic control was vectoring the aircraft for a visual approach. The aircraft was turned from the downwind leg onto something close to a base leg and cleared for the visual approach. On receiving the clearance, the first officer selected 1,900 ft in the altitude selector, because the aircraft was still outside the next fix on the approach. The crew were slowing the aircraft and configuring it for landing at the same time, and did not notice that the aircraft had descended to 1,600 ft. The ground proximity warning system then gave a "Caution, obstacle" alert, for a tower in line with the localiser. The crew kept visual contact throughout and continued the turn towards the approach course.
safe_outcome: The aircraft joined the approach course and landed without further incident. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: Another aircraft was crossing nearby. Both crews received TCAS resolution advisories and followed them, and the aircraft passed about 300 feet vertically and half a mile apart. A flight attendant on this aircraft was thrown against a galley cart during the manoeuvre and received a minor injury.

notes: Single narrative (first officer, pilot flying). Rule 3, removed: the stated primary reason (time compression from late configuration), the 'in retrospect' preference to slow and configure earlier, and 'overwhelmed'. Rule 5, moved to the safe ending: joining the approach course and the landing. Rule 6: airport, runway and fix name removed. Judgement calls: the report's 'caution obstacle alert off of the GPWS from the Tower in line with the LOC' is read as a GPWS obstacle alert caused by a tower (structure) on the localiser line; no ATC alert is coded in the result fields, which supports that reading, but it is an interpretation. 'Pseudo left base' rendered 'something close to a base leg'. The report does not say whether or how the crew climbed back; nothing was added. Day or night not coded and not inferable (12:01-18:00, January), so left out. Shared text is 153 words including the paragraph labels (147 without); the report is short and nothing was added. Bracket 'crossing': the aircraft went below its selected altitude in a turn and did not climb.
